observations.feature: Mound E, Area D and Mound F
observations.assertion: The author compares bicolour tablets from the workshop with H-773, H-774 and H-194 from Area D and Mound F, using shared inscriptions and colour.
observations.dating_basis: Interaction assigned by the author to 3B; independent dates for each older find not supplied here.
observations.uncertainty: Material resemblance and shared text are proposed links; mould identity, chemical groups and old-find contexts require checking.

observations.assertion: The author proposes strongly regulated production and a possible mint-like role for the workshop.
observations.dating_basis: Interpretation of the source's 3B assemblage.
observations.uncertainty: Restricted workshop area does not identify controller, city-wide monopoly, currency or labour payment; these are the source's hypotheses.

observations.feature: East Mound E, outside curtain wall 296, Trench 11
observations.assertion: Twenty-two incised steatite tablets comprise H-2218–H-2239; sixteen were in a clump, two nearby and four scattered.
observations.locator: Author p. 13, PDF 14; Figure 4; 24 October summary-v1.json
observations.dating_basis: Dumped debris lies after wall 296 and its revetment fill, before 3C material; relative deposition date.
observations.uncertainty: A clump is one related depositional observation; nearby members do not become observed clump members.

observations.assertion: Microscopic mould examination led the excavators to identify at least three cutting hands and common stroke order and cutting direction.
observations.locator: Author p. 15, PDF 16 and Figure 4 caption
observations.dating_basis: Manufacture timing and number of workshops remain unresolved.
observations.uncertainty: Three cutting hands are an attribution, not three independently dated workshops or institutions.

observations.assertion: Attachment, contents, independent quantity, use wear, cancellation and a recovered pouch are unreported for the 22 named tablets in this chapter.

observations.assertion: The excavators distinguish forty pre-firing vessel stamps H-1727–H-1766 from six separate clay tags H-1719–H-1724 and one unbaked stopper H-1725.
observations.dating_basis: PBG and long rectangular-seal typology assigned to 3C, ca. 2200–1900 BCE.
observations.uncertainty: Forty entries are not forty independent vessel batches; H-1741's export TAG classification conflicts with the source range.

observations.assertion: A stamp placed before firing became a persistent part of the vessel during manufacture.
observations.dating_basis: Manufacturing sequence established by pre-firing impression; no measured elapsed duration.
observations.uncertainty: This permits producer, commissioner or intended-use hypotheses; independently identified contents or issuer are absent.

observations.assertion: Six HARP tags were partly hardened by low firing; an unfired stopper survived because conservators intervened immediately.
observations.dating_basis: Secondary tag contexts do not distinguish deliberate archiving from later heating.
observations.uncertainty: Baked versus unbaked preservation changes observed sealing frequency; low recovered frequency is not a direct rate of closure use.

observations.uncertainty: Not a new six-object census addition; exact die, fabric and object aliases need original-page comparison.
